assessment_summary:
I inspected the installation left in the container and validated it by observing real software behavior, not just file existence.

Inspection: /workspace is the package root (git 7acedda, package.json name @seitenbau-dev/formulardesigner v1.0.2). Node/npm are installed (v24.21.0 / 11.19.0). /workspace/node_modules is populated (npm ls --depth=0 exits 0). The build output /workspace/dist exists and exactly matches the declared package entry points (main/module dist/formulardesigner.es.js, types dist/src/index.d.ts, ./types dist/src/types/index.d.ts, plus dist/assets/index.css). The example app at /workspace/example has its dependency linked to the library root via the `file:..` symlink, and it also has a completed production build under example/dist.

Behavioral validation: (1) Importing the built ESM bundle under Node (with a throw-away loader that stubs only the .css import, since a browser/Vite library cannot load CSS directly in Node) succeeds and exposes the documented `FormularDesigner` export. (2) Server-rendering that component with the guide's example empty form produces a substantial, well-formed KERN markup tree, proving the component initializes and renders, not merely that files exist. (3) The documented run path works: `npm run dev` in example brought Vite up on 5173; the root document returned 200 with the expected title, and every example source module and the entire library dependency graph (React, zustand, react-hook-form, use-sync-external-store, and the served library bundle/CSS) resolved with HTTP 200 and no transform/resolution errors. (4) The production build serves correctly via `vite preview` (HTML/JS/CSS all 200). (5) The documented ref API (`getModel`, `setDirtyForm`) is present both in the type declarations and the bundle. (6) A registry lookup confirms the guide's `npm install @seitenbau-dev/formulardesigner` package exists at the same version.

Limitations/uncertainty: Playwright E2E (`npm run test`) could not run because browser binaries are absent; installing them is prohibited by the validation boundaries, but E2E is not part of the guide's documented install/run workflow, so this does not indicate an incomplete installation. HTTP-level checks cannot confirm visual rendering in a real browser, but direct SSR execution of the component provides equivalent runtime evidence. The published-package install branch of the guide was not exercised directly (the repo-local `file:..` build path was), yet the registry confirms the package exists and the local build reproduces its entry points.

Overall, objective runtime evidence shows the library builds, imports, and renders, and the documented example application installs, starts, and serves successfully — the installation is complete and operational.
